innovations.name: Consumer
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. Dexcom set Q3 results for Oct 29 after the close and Hims for Nov 9; Abbott reports Oct 21. The FDA panel on Sydnexis's SYD-101 myopia drop is still set for Oct 30, and Oura has not set a new IPO date since postponing on Sep 29. No stage moves: these are dates, not new revenue or approvals.
innovations.for_you: DXCM (86.04) is 'Buy zone now', but it reports Oct 29: use a small tranche or wait, and do not sell a November put through the report. ABT (104.89) is above its 98.39 to 100.45 zone into Oct 21. HIMS (28.07) is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' and reports Nov 9.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.what: A Vox Brasil poll of 2,100 voters taken Oct 15 to 17 has Lula at 51% of valid votes to Flavio Bolsonaro's 49%, the first recent poll with Lula ahead (Rio Times). Datafolha (Oct 13 to 14) still has Bolsonaro 51% to 49%, and all recent polls are inside their margins of error. Betting markets were far more confident in Bolsonaro (77% to 78% on Oct 16), so the gap between polls and prices is the risk.
countries.for_you: No action until after Oct 25. NU (14.56) is 'Buy zone now', but a Lula win would likely hit NU, ITUB and BBD, while a Bolsonaro win is mostly priced. All are left out of both lists because the polls are a coin flip.

countries.name: European Union
countries.what: Reuters reported on Oct 17 that Rosneft's Ryazan refinery, which supplies Moscow, halted its main crude unit (CDU-6) after Ukraine's Oct 15 drone strike (Kyiv Independent). A suspected Ukrainian drone also set fire to the Surgut condensate stabilization plant in western Siberia on Oct 16 (Moscow Times). Fewer working Russian units means less Russian diesel for export, which keeps European fuel costs high into winter.
countries.for_you: No action. TTE has no buy zone verdict. This keeps diesel and inflation pressure on Europe, which supports more ECB hikes at the Oct 29 meeting and helps European banks (SAN, ING) more than industrials.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: On Oct 17 Iran's foreign minister said Tehran's seven day plan, sent through Qatar, still stands: the strait would reopen on day six if the US lifts its naval blockade and oil sanctions and agrees to a ceasefire that includes Lebanon (Tasnim). The US has rejected a return to the June terms. The same day the Revolutionary Guards claimed a second supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels hit a mine and stopped in the strait; there is no independent confirmation (Middle East Monitor).
countries.for_you: Oil faces two way risk at Monday's open: more mine claims push it up, a US reply to Iran's plan would push it down fast. If you hold energy swings, keep the dashboard stops (XOM 162.99, CVX 210.45, COP 135.75) and do not buy a gap up. FRO is left out of both lists: a reopening would ease freight rates, more attacks would raise them.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: Two surveys published Oct 18 expect the Bank of Korea to hold its 3.00% rate on Oct 22: 19 of 20 experts in a Seoul Economic Daily poll and all 11 in a MoneyToday poll. Most expect a 'hawkish hold' and another hike in November, sooner if the Fed signals a December hike.
countries.for_you: No action. A hold removes Thursday's surprise risk, but a November hike stays on the table, so Korean bank ADRs (KB 118.81, SHG 70.31) stay hurt. Wait for SK hynix on Oct 28 before any Korea or memory trade.
